sub_questions.q: Which models does the paper introduce?
sub_questions.answer: The paper introduces the Long-Short Term Memory Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (LSTMRNTN) and Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (GRURNTN).
sub_questions.quote: our proposed models, which are called a Long-Short Term Memory Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (LSTMRNTN) and Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (GRURNTN)

sub_questions.q: Which previous baseline models are used for comparison?
sub_questions.answer: The previous baseline models are GRURNN and LSTMRNN.
sub_questions.quote: we compared the performance from our baseline models GRURNN and LSTMRNN with our proposed GRURNTN and LSTMRNTN models.

sub_questions.q: On which language modeling tasks are the models evaluated?
sub_questions.answer: They are evaluated on word-level language modeling and character-level language modeling.
sub_questions.quote: We conducted experiments with our proposed models on word-level and character-level language modeling tasks

sub_questions.q: How much does each proposed model improve over its baseline on character-level language modeling?
sub_questions.answer: GRURNTN reduces test BPC from 1.39 to 1.33, which is 0.06 absolute / 4.32% relative, over GRURNN; LSTMRNTN reduces BPC from 1.37 to 1.34, which is 0.03 absolute / 2.22% relative, over LSTMRNN.
sub_questions.quote: GRURNTN reduced the BPC from 1.39 to 1.33 (0.06 absolute / 4.32% relative BPC) from the baseline GRURNN, and LSTMRNTN reduced the BPC from 1.37 to 1.34 (0.03 absolute / 2.22% relative BPC) from the baseline LSTMRNN.

sub_questions.q: How much does each proposed model improve over its baseline on word-level language modeling?
sub_questions.answer: GRURNTN reduces test PPL from 97.78 to 87.38, which is 10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative, over GRURNN; LSTMRNTN reduces PPL from 108.26 to 96.97, which is 11.29 absolute / 10.42% relative, over LSTMRNN.
sub_questions.quote: GRURNTN reduced the perplexity from 97.78 to 87.38 (10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative PPL) over the baseline GRURNN and LSTMRNTN reduced the perplexity from 108.26 to 96.97 (11.29 absolute / 10.42% relative PPL) over the baseline LSTMRNN.

sub_questions.q: Do the proposed models outperform the baseline models overall?
sub_questions.answer: Both proposed models outperformed the baseline models in character-level and word-level language modeling tasks with similar numbers of parameters.
sub_questions.quote: our proposed models outperformed the baseline models with a similar number of parameters in character-level language modeling and word-level language modeling tasks.
